title: Long GM — Q2 Beat + FY2026 Guidance Raised Second Time; Industrial Cycle Cheaply Priced
entry: Long $76–$82 at the July 21 open or any intraday dip toward $76–$78. GM reported Q2 FY2026 before the open on July 21: adjusted EPS $3.57 vs $3.13 consensus (14% beat), revenue $48.03B vs $47.01B (2.2% beat), and full-year adjusted EBIT guidance raised for the second time in 2026 to $14B–$16B (prior range $13.5B–$15.5B). Adjusted EPS full-year guidance raised to $12–$14 from $11.50–$13.50. The stock opened at $76.99 vs a pre-earnings close of $76.07 (+1.2%) — a muted reaction for a 14% EPS beat — creating the entry opportunity. Do NOT initiate above $84 (above near-term resistance, R:R degrades). Do NOT chase below $75 (wait for confirmation of support at post-earnings lows).
stop_loss: $71.50 daily close (~9.5% below $79 reference price) — at $71.50, either (1) the tariff escalation scenario has materialized (new 25% Mexico/Canada auto content tariff announced, reversing the cost-reduction thesis), (2) July auto retail data showed a pull-forward reversal in truck/SUV demand, or (3) GM issues a cautionary interim update on H2 EBIT trajectory. Below $71.50, the FY guidance raise is no longer credible and the entry premise is broken.
targets: $84 — Near-term technical resistance at the top of the July consolidation range; sell-side begins raising FY2026 EPS estimates toward $13.50 on the second consecutive guidance lift; Q3 EBIT tracking above midpoint of guidance range; cover 40% of position; +6.3% gain from $79 reference

$88 — Retest of the 52-week high ($87.62); third FY2026 guidance raise would trigger re-rating toward 7x forward earnings on $13 midpoint guide (implied fair value $91); momentum from declining EV losses and stable North America truck pricing supports multiple expansion; cover 40% of remaining position; +11.4% gain

risk_reward: 1:2.1 to Target 3 from $79 reference (risk $7.50; T3 reward $16.00)
catalyst: GM Q2 FY2026 results (reported before market open July 21) delivered the second consecutive guidance raise in a calendar year — a pattern that historically signals earnings momentum, not one-time beats. Adjusted EPS of $3.57 beat consensus of $3.13 by 14%; revenue of $48.03B beat $47.01B consensus by 2.2%. The full-year adjusted EBIT range moved to $14B–$16B (midpoint $15B) and adjusted EPS range to $12–$14 (midpoint $13), both raised $500M from prior guidance issued after Q1. CEO Mary Barra attributed the beat to stable North America pickup/SUV pricing, declining warranty expenses, and shrinking EV segment losses — all structurally positive inputs. Adjusted automotive free cash flow guidance raised to $9.5B–$11.5B. The muted initial stock reaction (+1.2% open) to a 14% EPS beat creates a second-order entry opportunity: the market has not yet priced the earnings quality improvement.
thesis:
GM's second consecutive FY guidance raise in 2026 signals a cost inflection, not a cyclical demand pull-forward. The distinction matters: demand pull-forwards (pre-tariff buying) compress future demand and compress multiples; cost reductions (lower warranty expense, shrinking EV losses) are durable improvements that support multiple expansion. CEO Barra's attribution to stable pricing + declining warranty + shrinking EV losses points to all three sources, with EV loss reduction being the most underappreciated. GM's EV segment losses were $3B+ in FY2024 and $2B+ in FY2025; if they fall toward $1.5B in FY2026 (consistent with the trajectory implied by the Q2 guidance raise), the GM auto business ex-EV is generating $16B+ EBIT — an industrial multiple of approximately 4x at the current stock price. This represents severe undervaluation relative to peers.

At $79, GM trades at approximately 6.1x the midpoint of raised FY2026 EPS guidance ($13). The S&P 500 industrials sector averages 18–20x forward earnings; even a discount to peers for auto-cycle risk and EV overhang implies a fair value of 8–10x, or $104–$130. The near-term thesis does not require full re-rating — it requires only that sell-side analysts raise FY2026 estimates from the current pre-earnings consensus (~$12) toward the new guidance midpoint ($13), which should push price targets from $90–$95 to $100–$110. The stock has historically responded to analyst target upgrades within 2–3 weeks of earnings.

The STEP ASIDE macro regime is a headwind — institutional money is not chasing cyclicals in a 30Y-above-5%/VIX-18 environment. But GM is not a purely rate-sensitive name; its primary sensitivity is to North America vehicle demand, which remains healthy at ~16M SAAR through Q2. The short-term catalyst is purely the earnings quality signal, which plays out over a 2–4 week analyst upgrade cycle regardless of macro regime.

The counter-party is the GM bear who argues: (1) the Q2 beat was driven by Q1 pull-forward demand ahead of tariff implementation; H2 demand will disappoint as that demand was borrowed from future quarters; (2) GM's Mexico and Canada sourcing exposure means any escalation in USMCA tariff enforcement creates a direct cost spike that reverses the guidance trajectory; (3) the muted +1.2% open on a 14% beat means institutional investors — who know the GM story better than anyone — are not buying the guidance raise narrative. These are legitimate concerns, which is why position size is 3% and the stop at $71.50 is tighter than the 10% typical for a medium-conviction idea.
bull_case: Sell-side upgrades GM price targets from $90–$95 to $105–$115 by July 25 on the second guidance raise. Goldman, JPM, and Morgan Stanley all have underweight-to-neutral positions that flip to buy — institutional accumulation pushes GM toward $87–$89 (52-week high retest) by August 1. EV loss update at Q3 earnings confirms a below-$1.5B trajectory for FY2026, re-rating GM toward $100+.
bear_case: USMCA tariff enforcement announcement in August targets GM's Mexico truck production specifically. H2 North America vehicle demand tracks below Q1 pull-forward-inflated pace. GM's H2 EBIT trajectory decelerates, triggering a pre-Q3-earnings guidance withdrawal. Stock falls from $79 toward $71 stop. Exit cleanly at stop.
invalidation: $71.50 GM daily close; OR White House announces 25%+ tariff specifically on Mexico-assembled light trucks or SUVs (GM's highest-margin vehicles); OR July/August auto sales data shows more than 10% MoM decline in North America truck/SUV volume (pull-forward reversion confirmed); OR GM issues interim cautionary update on H2 EBIT trajectory before Q3 earnings
